In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the German‐Polish cooperation has been very fruitful in the field of hair pigmentation disorders, especially in the case of the side effects of chemotherapy.
the German‐Polish cooperation in the field of hair pigmentation disorders was initiated by Kostanecki in the 1930s and continued by the Płonka group in the 1960s and 1970s.
Kostanecki was the founder of the field of hair pigmentation disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that hair pigmentation is a very complex process, involving several genes and pathways.
we have demonstrated that the hair follicle is a target for chemotherapy, and the hair follicle cells are very sensitive to cytostatics.
we have shown that the hair follicle is a target of cytotoxic drugs and that it is a target of choice for the development of new strategies to prevent chemotherapy‐induced hair loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the use of the new method for the analysis of the data of a large number of patients with hair loss due to cancer treatment is possible.
the use of a new, non‐invasive, and reliable method for measuring hair color in vivo is an essential tool for the study of hair pigmentation disorders.
